Edwardsville, 1962

Saturday afternoon, 21 July 1962, in the seat of Madison County, Illinois. You start on North Main Street in front of the county jail: the sheriff's house of 1869, Second Empire with a mansard roof, and behind it the jail, the iron cage of 1869 and the steel cells of 1904. Walk in through the front door and through the back of the hall into the jail; or go anywhere in town, downtown, the courthouse, the Wildey, Leclaire and the fields beyond.

Built from the records: the USGS elevations; the USGS map of 1954 (aerial photographs of 1952), which decides which of today's buildings and streets stood then, and puts back houses that are gone; the Sanborn fire insurance maps of 1930-47 for downtown and the jail's outline; and E. W. Bowles's history of the jail (1960) for its cells and fittings. No plans of the jail survive, so its rooms are reconstructed as such jails were built. The blue i points say what is known and what is guessed.
